tools.name: Sewing needle
tools.description: A hand-sewing needle suited to the fabric.

tools.name: Scissors
tools.description: Small sharp scissors for cutting thread.

tools.name: Pins or clips
tools.description: Hold fabric edges together while you sew.

tools.name: Plain bar soap
tools.description: A tiny amount can help a sticking zipper.

guides.title: Bring back a missing button
guides.summary: One small stitch job. A favorite shirt back in rotation.

steps.title: Find the right spot
steps.body: Match the button to the buttonhole and mark its position. Check that the surrounding fabric is intact.

steps.title: Thread your needle
steps.body: Use matching thread and knot its end. Place the button on the marked spot.

steps.title: Secure the button
steps.body: Follow the linked illustrated guide to stitch through each pair of holes several times. Keep the button aligned.

steps.title: Tie off and test
steps.body: Secure the thread on the underside, trim it, then check that the button fastens comfortably.

guides.caution: Needles are sharp. This plan is for adult clothing; loose small parts need professional attention on clothing for children under three.

guides.title: Close an open seam
guides.summary: A neat hand stitch for a seam that has come apart.
guides.symptom: Stitching has opened; fabric is still intact

steps.title: Check the fabric
steps.body: Find both ends of the open seam. If the cloth itself has torn, choose a patch repair instead.

steps.title: Align the edges
steps.body: Bring the folded seam edges together and hold them with pins or clips. Match the original seam line.

steps.title: Work a ladder stitch
steps.body: Use the original illustrated guide to alternate small stitches between the two folded edges. Pull gently to close the gap.

steps.title: Secure your stitches
steps.body: Tie off at intact stitching, trim the thread, remove pins, and gently check that the seam holds.

guides.caution: Stop if the fabric frays or tears under tension. Delicate, technical, or load-bearing seams may need a specialist.

guides.title: Free a sticking zipper
guides.summary: A gentle first check before you replace the whole zip.
guides.symptom: Zipper sticks; teeth and slider are intact

steps.title: Look before pulling
steps.body: Check whether lining, thread, or debris is trapped in the slider. Do not force a damaged zipper.

steps.title: Release trapped fabric
steps.body: Ease the slider backwards and gently free the caught material with tweezers. Stop if it resists.

steps.title: Try a little soap
steps.body: On an inconspicuous area first, test plain bar soap for marks. Following the source guide, apply a small amount to the teeth.

steps.title: Test gently
steps.body: Move the slider slowly. Wipe away residue. Broken teeth or a separating zipper need a different repair.

guides.caution: Do not use this plan on broken teeth or a split slider. Test soap on hidden material first; it can leave marks.

source.name: iFixit · Repair a zipper with soap

guides.title: Give a cushion another chapter
guides.summary: Close a small open seam without a sewing machine.
guides.symptom: Cushion seam has opened; cover is undamaged

steps.title: Check the opening
steps.body: Make sure this is an open seam rather than torn fabric. Keep any loose filling safely inside.

steps.title: Fold and align
steps.body: Follow the original seam folds and hold the edges together with clips. Avoid trapping filling in the seam.

steps.title: Sew the gap closed
steps.body: Follow the linked ladder-stitch guide, alternating small stitches on either edge. Draw the thread snug without puckering.

steps.title: Secure and check
steps.body: Knot at intact stitching and trim. Remove clips and gently check the seam before using the cushion.

guides.caution: For decorative cushion covers only. Do not use this plan for weighted, heated, or safety-related products.

guides.title: Mend a tote’s open side seam
guides.summary: A simple hand repair for an everyday fabric bag.
guides.symptom: Side seam has opened; no tear in the fabric
materials: Strong thread suited to the bag

steps.title: Empty and inspect
steps.body: Check that only the seam stitching has failed. Handle attachments or torn material need a different plan.

steps.title: Align the original seam
steps.body: Turn the bag inside out. Clip both edges together along the original seam line.

steps.title: Hand-stitch the opening
steps.body: Follow the linked hand-seam repair guide with small, even stitches. Anchor the repair in intact stitching at both ends.

steps.title: Check before carrying
steps.body: Secure the thread and turn the bag right side out. Start with light contents and inspect the repair.

guides.caution: Not for climbing gear, baby carriers, or heavy loads. A handle attachment failure should be assessed by a repairer.

guides.title: Save a coat’s loose button
guides.summary: Make room for thick fabric with a thread shank.
guides.symptom: Loose four-hole button on thick adult clothing

steps.title: Match the button
steps.body: Make sure the button fits its hole and the attachment area is sound.

steps.title: Prepare for thick fabric
steps.body: Follow the source’s illustrated shank technique. The gap under the button allows thick cloth to fasten.

steps.title: Stitch and form the shank
steps.body: Secure the button through its holes, then form the thread shank exactly as shown in the linked guide.

steps.title: Secure and try it on
steps.body: Knot securely, trim excess thread, and test the fastening without stretching the surrounding cloth.

guides.caution: Sharp needle and small parts. Adult garments only; clothing for children under three needs professional repair.

source.name: Patagonia / iFixit · Button on Heavy Fabric
